paper.title: AFA-BANDIT: Provably Near-Optimal Online Multi-Feature Classification Under Budget Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Online active feature acquisition as predictor-coupled combinatorial Bandits with Knapsacks
unmapped: Actions are subsets of V features (each containing a free set S_0); the reward is the 0/1 correctness of a learned classifier on the acquired features, so expected rewards evolve over time as the predictor is updated (they are not additive over features)
Choosing a subset reveals the rewards of all of its own subsets (the inclusion order acts as a feedback graph), and the true label is revealed after each prediction
Feature acquisition costs c_v are known to the learner; there is a single global budget B
Data come from a parametric mixture distribution with K classes, for which the empirical mean is an unbiased estimator of the parameters
The expected reward is L-smooth in the classifier parameter, and the learner knows L
settings.definition_quote: We consider online multiclass classification over $T$ rounds ($T$ is known). At round $t$, an example $(X_t,Y_t)$ is drawn from an unknown distribution $\mathcal{P}$, where $Y_t\in[K]$ is the label, and $X_t=(X_{t,1},\ldots,X_{t,V})$ is an observation consisting of $V$ features. ... Feature $v$ has a known acquisition cost $c_v\geq 0$. ... Acquisitions are subject to a global budget $B$ over the $T$ rounds.

algorithms.name: Combinatorial primal-dual (dimension-aware UCB + OMD dual update)

symbols.OPT_LP: value of the LP relaxation benchmark (optimal static policy)

conditions: Assumption 1: observations, rewards in [0,1] and costs c(S) in [0,1] are bounded
The expected reward is L-Lipschitz smooth with respect to theta
Data come from a parametric mixture with unbiased empirical-mean estimators

source.label: THM:REGRET_UB
source.quote: Let the reward achieved by the optimal static policy be $\OPTLP$, and suppose Assumption~\ref{assump:conditions} holds. Then the regret \eqref{eq:regret} of the proposed algorithm satisfies \begin{equation*} \regret(T)\leq \mathcal{O}\left(\sqrt{\frac{2^{V}K}{\sqrt{V}}\OPTLP}+\OPTLP\sqrt{\frac{1}{B}}\right). \end{equation*}

results.notes: Regret is defined as OPT_LP - E[REW] (the BwK benchmark); it is recorded as expected regret against the LP-relaxation feasible policy. The result applies only to the combinatorial algorithm, not to LP-Chain. Per round, the algorithm takes an argmax over all 2^V subsets, so the computation is exponential in V. The proof is informal in places (e.g. it states the OMD regret is O(T) but then uses sqrt(T)).
